prompt: Find the $x$-coordinate of the inflection point of $f(x) = x^3 - 6x^2 + 9x + 2$.
hint: An inflection point is where concavity changes, which is where $f''$ changes sign. Differentiate twice.

hints.text: An inflection point is where concavity changes, which is where $f''$ changes sign. Differentiate twice.
$6x - 12 = 0$ gives $x = 2$. Since $f''$ is negative left of $2$ and positive right of $2$, concavity really does flip there.

explanation: Concavity changes, so $x = 2$ is the inflection point. (Its $y$-value is $f(2) = 8 - 24 + 18 + 2 = 4$.)

alternativeExplanations.title: Midpoint of the two extremes
steps: $f'(x) = 3(x - 1)(x - 3)$, so $f$ has a local max at $x = 1$ and a local min at $x = 3$.
Every cubic is symmetric about its inflection point, which sits exactly halfway between its two turning points.
